I need you to output a complete, well-structured JSON object for a revised research idea. I will give you all the details — your job is to assemble them into clean JSON with no markdown wrapping, just the raw JSON object.

Here is the complete revised idea:

```json
{
  "change_type": "minor",
  "title": "VLA-SSD: Do VLAs Know Which Demonstrations Are Good? Self-Referential Quality Scoring from Pretrained Representations",
  "core_problem": "Offline VLA fine-tuning on heterogeneous demonstration datasets is bottlenecked by the absence of reliable, annotation-free quality signals. Existing approaches each impose substantial external dependencies: GVL (ICLR 2025 Spotlight) achieves zero-shot value estimation across 300+ tasks but requires per-frame inference from Gemini-scale VLMs; TOPReward (Feb 2026) achieves 0.947 VOC zero-shot but requires a separate 4-8B VLM at scoring time; SCIZOR (ICRA 2026) uses external DINO-V2 features not adapted to the action domain and applies hard binary filtering that discards gradient signal; RINSE (ICML 2025) provides architecture-agnostic trajectory smoothness scoring via SAL/TED metrics without any learned features; influence-function methods (CUPID, CoRL 2025; QoQ, arXiv 2603.09056) require evaluation rollouts or curated validation datasets; PROGRESSOR (ICCV 2025) requires external pretraining on EPIC-KITCHENS video; and ProgressVLA (Microsoft, March 2026) trains a separate progress estimator on large-scale video-text datasets. Online methods (SRPO, VLAC) require environment interaction entirely. Notably, a survey of ICLR 2026 VLA submissions reveals that data curation remains a critically underrepresented problem despite being widely acknowledged as a bottleneck. A fundamental question remains: do VLA models, through large-scale pretraining on action-prediction tasks, already encode sufficient task-progress information in their own internal representations to score demonstration quality — enabling a fully self-referential pipeline with zero external models, zero additional inference cost, and zero annotation requirements?",
  "opportunity": "Recent mechanistic interpretability work provides moderate but encouraging evidence that VLA representations encode task-relevant information. The Emergent World Representations study (arXiv 2509.24559) demonstrates that linear probes on OpenVLA hidden states achieve R²=0.667 for state transition vector prediction (K=30 setting), confirming meaningful task-dynamic information is accessible in VLA feature space — though this falls well short of perfect prediction and concerns continuous state transitions rather than discrete progress. Complementarily, Probing OpenVLA for Symbolic States (arXiv 2502.04558) shows >90% accuracy for discrete symbolic state classification (binary properties like is_grasped, is_on_table) on LIBERO-Spatial, demonstrating that VLA representations linearly encode task-relevant binary predicates. Most directly, the mechanistic study 'Not All Features Are Created Equal' (arXiv 2603.19233) reports that π0.5 expert pathway features achieve R²=0.45 for continuous state prediction and AUC=0.93 for success prediction, with expert pathways consistently outperforming VLM pathways for motor-relevant information — directly demonstrating discriminative capacity in VLA features for quality-related judgments. SAE analyses (arXiv 2603.19183) reveal that 97-99% of individual sparse dictionary features are memorized on LIBERO-tuned models, but DROID-pretrained models show only 89.19% memorization, and critically, aggregate hidden-state vectors remain discriminative for state-level properties despite individual-feature memorization. The OpenGVL benchmark (arXiv 2509.17321) further reveals that open-source VLMs achieve only ~70% of closed-source VLM performance on temporal progress estimation, suggesting that VLA-internal features — which are natively adapted to the action domain — may offer competitive or superior signal without requiring external VLM inference. This creates a testable opportunity: if VLA features can support temporal distance estimation (frame-pair relative progress) beyond what positional embeddings alone provide, and if this signal outperforms both generic visual features (DINO-V2) and simple trajectory geometry (RINSE), then the same model being fine-tuned can score its own training data at zero marginal cost.",
  "landscape": "The demonstration curation space for VLA fine-tuning has rapidly expanded across seven complementary approaches: (1) **Zero-shot VLM value estimation**: GVL (ICLR 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2411.04549) poses value estimation as temporal ordering of shuffled video frames using Gemini-1.5-Pro, achieving zero-shot value prediction across 300+ tasks with Value-Order Correlation (VOC) as the metric. Applied to dataset filtering and advantage-weighted regression (AWR) on real ALOHA tasks. Limitation: requires per-frame API calls to a Gemini-scale VLM, with no reported compute cost analysis. OpenGVL (arXiv 2509.17321) benchmarks open-source VLMs on this task, finding they achieve ~70% of closed-source performance. TOPReward (Feb 2026, arXiv 2602.19313) extracts zero-shot progress from VLM token probabilities (0.947 VOC on Qwen3-VL), applied to advantage-weighted fine-tuning of pi0. Both require a separate large VLM at scoring time. (2) **Self-supervised visual curation**: SCIZOR (ICRA 2026, arXiv 2505.22626) trains a temporal distance classifier on frozen DINO-V2 features to estimate progress, then hard-filters low-quality timesteps and removes redundant data via joint state-action deduplication. Achieves 5.4% improvement on RoboMimic, 8.1% on OXE-Magic-Soup, and 32.9% on Sirius-Fleet real-robot tasks. Limitations: external visual features without action-domain adaptation; hard binary filtering discards gradient signal; tested primarily on Octo, not modern VLAs. VLA-SSD directly extends SCIZOR's temporal distance classification framework to VLA-internal representations, testing whether action-domain adaptation through VLA pretraining provides superior progress signals, and replaces hard filtering with soft reward weighting grounded in iw-SFT theory. (3) **Trajectory geometry heuristics**: RINSE (ICML 2025, arXiv 2604.23000) uses Spectral Arc Length (SAL, frequency-domain smoothness) and Trajectory-Envelope Distance (TED, spatial contact-aware geometry) for architecture-agnostic demo scoring. Achieves 16% higher success with 1/6 data on RoboMimic, 20% improvement with 1/2 data in real-world tasks, and 5.6% mean success improvement on LIBERO-10 via STRAP integration. Requires zero model access or learned features. This is the critical lower bound: if learned features cannot beat pure trajectory geometry, feature-based scoring is unjustified. (4) **External progress estimators**: PROGRESSOR (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2411.17764) learns a task-agnostic reward function pretrained on EPIC-KITCHENS for goal-conditioned RL. ProgressVLA (Microsoft, March 2026, arXiv 2603.27670) pre-trains a dedicated progress estimator on large-scale unsupervised video-text robotic datasets (0.07 prediction residual, zero-shot real-world transfer), integrated into a diffusion VLA with inverse dynamics guidance. Both require external pretraining data/models. (5) **Influence-function curation**: CUPID (CoRL 2025) and QoQ (arXiv 2603.09056) use REINFORCE-style influence estimation for trajectory-level filtering. QoQ achieves 23.2%/30.0% improvements on GR00T N1 VLA. Both require evaluation rollouts or curated validation sets and provide only trajectory-level granularity. (6) **External reward models**: Robometer (RSS 2026, arXiv 2603.02115) trains Qwen3-VL-4B on 1M+ trajectories for dense per-frame progress with strong zero-shot transfer (Kendall tau=0.66 OOD). Requires a separate 4-8B VLM at scoring time. (7) **Online self-improvement**: SRPO (arXiv 2511.15605) uses the model's own successful rollouts for self-referential optimization (48.9→99.2% on LIBERO). PLD (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2511.00091) uses residual RL to probe VLA failure regions, collect recovery data, and distill back via SFT (99% on LIBERO, 50%+ gains on SimplerEnv). VLAC (arXiv 2509.15937) integrates a dense progress critic into an online RL loop. All require environment interaction. (8) **Weighted BC frameworks**: VACO (ICLR 2025) uses a meta-scoring network for bi-level weighted BC on D4RL. iw-SFT (arXiv 2507.12856) proves that SFT on curated data maximizes a lower bound on the RL objective, tightened by importance weighting — providing theoretical justification for quality-weighted BC as a principled approach. **Gap**: No work has investigated whether VLA-internal features — uniquely adapted to the action domain through pretraining and already computed during the forward pass — can serve as a self-referential progress estimator that (a) beats trajectory geometry heuristics (RINSE), justifying learned features, (b) matches or exceeds external VLM scoring (GVL/TOPReward) on task-specific data, and (c) does so at zero marginal cost since features are a byproduct of the fine-tuning forward pass.",
  "approach": "VLA-SSD is a three-stage offline pipeline that tests a mechanistic hypothesis — VLA pretrained representations encode task-progress information sufficient for self-referential demonstration scoring — and operationalizes positive findings into a theoretically-grounded curriculum-weighted fine-tuning method. The theoretical foundation comes from iw-SFT (arXiv 2507.12856), which proves that SFT on quality-scored data maximizes a lower bound on the RL objective, tightened by importance weighting; VLA-SSD's quality scores serve as the importance weights, making the pipeline provably principled rather than heuristic.

**Stage 1 — Temporal Distance Probing with Positional Embedding Controls**: Extract frozen hidden-state representations h_l(t) from every transformer layer l of the pretrained VLA (OpenVLA 7B as primary, π0.5 as validation) for each demonstration timestep. Train lightweight probes at each layer using TWO complementary targets designed to be robust against positional embedding shortcuts:

(a) **Temporal distance classification** (primary target): Given a pair of frames (t_i, t_j) from the same trajectory, predict relative progress Δp = |t_j - t_i|/T from feature differences h_l(t_j) - h_l(t_i). This forces the probe to compare semantic content between two frames rather than recovering absolute temporal position from a single frame, directly mitigating the positional embedding shortcut. This explicitly extends SCIZOR's temporal distance classification framework — which uses frozen DINO-V2 features — to the VLA's own internal representations, testing whether action-domain adaptation through VLA pretraining provides superior progress signals.

(b) **Sub-task predicate classification** (secondary target, LIBERO only): LIBERO provides BDDL goal predicates (e.g., is_grasped, is_on_table, is_in_drawer) checkable at every simulator timestep. Train binary classifiers on VLA features to predict sub-task completion milestones. These are discrete semantic properties that cannot be predicted from positional embeddings, providing the strongest evidence for genuine task understanding.

(c) **Positional embedding control experiment** (probe-level only, not full pipeline): Train identical probes on positional embeddings alone (extracted from the same transformer layers but with content features zeroed out / using only the position component). If VLA content features significantly outperform positional-embedding-only probes, this confirms the signal comes from task-semantic representations, not temporal position recovery.

Probe architecture: single linear layer + sigmoid for classification, ~50K params each. 80/20 train/validation split within the demonstration set. Rank layers by validation performance (Spearman ρ for temporal distance, AUC for sub-task predicates); select best layer l* automatically. Based on arXiv 2603.19233, expert pathway features (PG5, PG11 equivalent) are hypothesized most informative, but selection is fully data-driven.

**Critical controlled ablations** (run in parallel):
- **DINO-V2 (ViT-L/14) baseline**: Extract DINO-V2 features from the same observations, train identical probes — isolates the effect of action-domain adaptation.
- **RINSE baseline**: Compute SAL and TED scores on the same trajectories — tests whether learned features beat trajectory geometry heuristics. If RINSE matches or exceeds our probes, the 'VLA features encode progress' narrative is undermined.
- **DINO-V2 Fallback**: If no VLA layer achieves Spearman ρ > 0.3 on temporal distance AND no layer achieves AUC > 0.7 on sub-task predicates, switch to DINO-V2 features for subsequent stages and report this as a negative mechanistic finding.

**Stage 2 — Hierarchical Quality Scoring**: Use the temporal distance probe from l* to compute per-timestep progress estimates by anchoring relative to the first frame: q_t = probe_{l*}(h_{l*}(t) - h_{l*}(0)). Derive trajectory-level quality Q(τ) = α * q_T + β * mono(τ) + γ * mean(q_t), combining terminal progress (endpoint quality), progress monotonicity (fraction of consecutive timesteps with increasing estimated progress), and average progress. Default weights: α=0.5, β=0.3, γ=0.2. Compute timestep-level reward weights w_t = q_t * Q(τ). Apply temperature-controlled normalization for the trajectory component. On LIBERO, additionally compute sub-task milestone coverage as a trajectory quality signal.

**Stage 3 — Curriculum-Weighted LoRA Fine-Tuning**: Fine-tune the VLA with LoRA (rank 16-64) using weighted BC loss with a curriculum temperature schedule that starts permissive and progressively sharpens quality weighting over training. Specifically, define a temperature parameter τ(epoch) that decreases linearly from τ_max to τ_min over training: w_t^(epoch) = softmax(q_t / τ(epoch)), where τ_max = 2.0 (near-uniform early training, allowing the model to learn from all demonstrations) and τ_min = 0.5 (sharp quality weighting in later epochs, focusing gradient signal on high-quality timesteps). The curriculum rationale: early uniform training establishes broad behavioral coverage, while progressive sharpening concentrates fine-tuning on the most informative demonstrations — analogous to curriculum learning in knowledge distillation (Curriculum Temperature, arXiv 2211.16231) and grounded by iw-SFT's theoretical result that tighter importance weighting progressively tightens the RL objective lower bound. The loss at each epoch: L = Σ_t w_t^(epoch) * ||a_t - π_θ(o_t, l)||². Unlike SCIZOR's hard filtering, soft reward weighting preserves gradient signal from all timesteps proportional to quality. Unlike GVL+AWR, no external VLM is needed — features come from the model being fine-tuned. Probes are trained once on pretrained features and frozen; all quality scores are computed before fine-tuning begins, ensuring no circular dependency.

**Evaluation Protocol**:

*Primary benchmarks* (in main paper): (1) RoboMimic Multi-Human (300 naturally mixed-quality demos from 6 operators of varied skill, Can and Square tasks). Validates quality scoring on natural distribution. Verify scores correlate with operator skill levels — the RoboMimic MH dataset organizes 50 demos per operator across 3 skill tiers (worse/okay/better); operator group membership is verifiable via filter keys using `get_dataset_info.py` and the known sequential collection structure. (2) LIBERO-Long with controlled noise injection (action jitter σ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, trajectory truncation at {50%, 75%}). Probes trained exclusively on clean data, then evaluated on mixed clean+noisy demonstrations — tests whether scoring generalizes beyond the noise distribution seen during probe training.

*Robustness benchmarks* (in appendix): LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2510.13626; 10,030 tasks across 7 perturbation dimensions) and LIBERO-PRO (arXiv 2510.03827). Report robustness gap Δ between nominal LIBERO success and perturbed-suite success.

*Scale validation* (in appendix): DROID subsets with natural variable-quality teleoperation, where SAE analysis shows more general features (10.81% vs 2.63% on LIBERO).

*π0.5 validation* (in appendix): Replicate core probing experiments (Stage 1) and one primary benchmark fine-tuning on π0.5 to validate generalization across VLA architectures.

**Baselines** (6 core + 2 appendix):

Core (main paper):
1. Vanilla BC (unweighted)
2. RINSE (SAL+TED trajectory geometry, no features) — critical lower bound
3. SCIZOR-style (DINO-V2 + temporal distance + hard filtering)
4. DINO-V2 + our curriculum-weighted pipeline (ablation isolating feature source)
5. GVL-style (open-source VLM scoring via OpenGVL protocol + AWR)
6. VLA-SSD without curriculum (static τ=1.0, ablating the curriculum contribution)

Appendix:
7. Oracle scoring (ground-truth operator labels/noise levels)
8. TOPReward (external VLM + AWR)

**Key metrics**: success rate on nominal and perturbed benchmarks, robustness gap Δ, probe Spearman ρ for temporal distance by layer (mechanistic), sub-task AUC by layer, quality score Kendall tau with ground-truth labels, VLA-feature vs. DINO-V2 vs. positional-embedding probe performance comparison (probe-level), VLA-feature vs. RINSE scoring comparison, curriculum ablation (with/without temperature schedule), compute overhead comparison (FLOPs, wall-clock, API cost).",

  "description": "We investigate a mechanistic question with direct practical implications: do Vision-Language-Action models already know which demonstrations are good? VLA-SSD (Self-Scored Demonstration Distillation) systematically probes pretrained VLA representations to determine whether they encode sufficient task-progress information for self-referential demonstration quality estimation — and if so, operationalizes this into a theoretically-grounded curriculum-weighted fine-tuning pipeline with zero external dependencies. Methodologically, VLA-SSD directly extends SCIZOR's (ICRA 2026) temporal distance classification framework — which uses frozen DINO-V2 features — to the VLA's own internal representations, testing whether action-domain adaptation through VLA pretraining provides superior progress signals; it additionally replaces SCIZOR's hard binary filtering with soft reward weighting grounded in iw-SFT theory (arXiv 2507.12856), which proves quality-weighted SFT optimizes a tighter lower bound on the RL objective.

VLA-SSD proceeds in three stages:

(1) Train lightweight probes on frozen VLA hidden states at every layer using temporal distance classification (predicting relative progress between frame pairs, robust to positional embedding shortcuts) as the primary target, and sub-task predicate classification (BDDL milestone completion on LIBERO) as a secondary semantic target. A critical positional-embedding-only control experiment (probe-level) isolates whether progress signal comes from task semantics or temporal position recovery. Parallel DINO-V2 probes control for action-domain adaptation effects. An automated layer-selection protocol identifies the most informative layers (hypothesized to be expert pathway layers based on arXiv 2603.19233's finding that π0.5 expert features achieve AUC=0.93 for success prediction).

(2) Construct hierarchical quality scores combining terminal progress, progress monotonicity, and average progress at trajectory and timestep levels.

(3) Apply curriculum-weighted LoRA fine-tuning with a temperature schedule that starts permissive (τ_max=2.0, near-uniform weights) and progressively sharpens to quality-focused (τ_min=0.5), where each timestep's gradient contribution is w_t^(epoch) = softmax(q_t / τ(epoch)). This curriculum — broad behavioral coverage first, then quality concentration — is grounded in iw-SFT's theoretical result that progressively tightening importance weights tightens the RL objective lower bound.

The core empirical question is three-fold: (a) Do VLA features encode progress beyond what positional embeddings provide? (b) Do VLA-internal features, adapted to the action domain through pretraining, outperform both generic visual features (DINO-V2) and simple trajectory geometry heuristics (RINSE)? (c) Does the resulting curriculum-weighted training produce policies that are both more successful and more robust under perturbation? We evaluate primarily on RoboMimic Multi-Human (300 naturally mixed-quality demos with verified operator skill tier labels) and LIBERO-Long with controlled noise injection, with LIBERO-Plus/PRO robustness analysis and DROID scale validation in appendix. OpenVLA 7B serves as the primary VLA with π0.5 validation in appendix. Six core baselines span vanilla BC, RINSE trajectory geometry (critical lower bound), SCIZOR, DINO-V2 ablation, GVL-style open-source VLM scoring, and curriculum ablation (static weights). The evidence base for VLA feature discriminativeness is moderate but encouraging: R²=0.667 for state transition prediction (arXiv 2509.24559), R²=0.45 for state prediction and AUC=0.93 for success prediction from π0.5 expert pathways (arXiv 2603.19233), >90% for discrete symbolic state classification (arXiv 2502.04558). Even negative results — VLA features underperforming RINSE's trajectory geometry — constitute valuable findings about VLA representation limits and the sufficiency of simple heuristics.",

}
```

**Stage 1 — Temporal Distance Probing with Positional Embedding Controls**: Extract frozen hidden-state representations h_l(t) from every transformer layer l of the pretrained VLA (OpenVLA 7B as primary, π0.5 as validation) for each demonstration timestep. (a) **Temporal distance classification** (primary target): Given a pair of frames (t_i, t_j) from the same trajectory, predict relative progress Δp = |t_j - t_i|/T from feature differences h_l(t_j) - h_l(t_i). (b) **Sub-task predicate classification** (secondary target, LIBERO only): LIBERO provides BDDL goal predicates (e.g., is_grasped, is_on_table, is_in_drawer) checkable at every simulator timestep. Train binary classifiers on VLA features to predict sub-task completion milestones. These are discrete semantic properties that cannot be predicted from positional embeddings, providing the strongest evidence for genuine task understanding.

(c) **Positional embedding control experiment** (probe-level only, not full pipeline): Train identical probes on positional embeddings alone (extracted from the same transformer layers but with content features zeroed out / using only the position component). Probe architecture: single linear layer + sigmoid for classification, ~50K params each. 80/20 train/validation split within the demonstration set.
